key_fields.sql: select z.borough, count(*) as touches from lake.trips t join ops.zones z on z.locationid = t.pulocationid or z.locationid = t.dolocationid group by z.borough order by z.borough
key_fields.claim: An OR inside the JOIN condition cannot use a hash join; the engine falls back to a nested-loop style join, which is far more expensive than two equi-joins. (matched: inner join ops.zones z on z.locationid = t.pulocationid or z.locationid = t.dolocationid)

value.sql: SELECT z.Borough, SUM(cnt) AS touches FROM (SELECT Borough, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM ops.zones z JOIN lake.trips t ON z.LocationID = t.PULocationID GROUP BY z.Borough UNION ALL SELECT Borough, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM ops.zones z JOIN lake.trips t ON z.LocationID = t.DOLocationID GROUP BY z.Borough) z GROUP BY z.Borough ORDER BY z.Borough
value.change_summary: Split the OR join into two separate equi-joins on PULocationID and DOLocationID, aggregated each side, then combined with UNION ALL and a final aggregation to preserve exact counts per borough.
